correctness.rationale: For each fixed toral tuple the commutator equations are the two-by-two minors between the evaluated weight row and the corresponding radical row. There are q radical choices for a nonzero weight row and q^r for a zero weight row. Expansion over subsets forces all toral coordinates to annihilate the selected weights, giving q^{r(d−rank S)} choices and the stated matroid formula. Uniform ranks give the binomial grouping; at r=1 the count is q^{m+d}. In the pair variety the locus with no vanishing weight rows is a rank-m vector bundle over a nonempty open subset of H² and has irreducible closure Y of dimension 2d+m. Away from H²=0 the vanishing rows are indexed by fewer than d independent weights, so their proportionality equations can be achieved on a one-parameter deformation into the open bundle. This gives the set-theoretic union Y∪E². To decide the small-m case, take B with ker B=im A, where A is the m-by-d weight matrix. Any m−d columns of B are independent because a dependency supported there would give a vector in im A annihilated on a complementary set of d independent weights. For m<2d, deleting any column of the stacked matrix K(U) leaves full row rank on a common dense open set: partition the remaining columns into two groups of size at least m−d and use one radical coordinate on each group for the full-rank specialization. The kernel then contains a vector with all coordinates nonzero, lifting the two scaled radical columns to im A. This produces a straight-line deformation into the open bundle, so E²⊆Y. When m=d the zero-row B gives the same conclusion immediately. For m≥2d, E² cannot be contained in Y: its dimension is at least that of Y, and at equality containment would force equality of irreducible closed sets, impossible since Y contains nonzero toral pairs. This independently confirms the component threshold and both dimensions. The supplied full-column-rank K(U) exclusion is consistent with it. Fresh enumeration of the actual row-minor equations matched 21 subset-rank comparisons, including nonuniform spanning weights and U_{2,4} over F₃. In the latter case the counts for arities 1, 2, 3 were 729, 18225, 657801. The checks can be replayed by enumerating toral tuples and all candidate length-r radical rows over the prime field, testing every minor and summing the products of row counts.
residual_risks: The arithmetic census is conditional on representability over the specified field and does not recover the full matroid or count orbits.
E² is the zero-toral fiber, not the square of the Lie center; this terminology does not affect the proof.
The geometry is over an algebraic closure for the reduced pair variety. The finite checks do not imply any scheme-theoretic or all-arity geometric statement.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A sharp threshold in a nilradical is not a theorem about the diagonal semidirect product with nonzero weights: the former is nilpotent, whereas a nonzero weight gives some adjoint action with nonzero eigenvalue in the latter. Borel classifications use root-system hypotheses rather than arbitrary uniform weight representations. Low-dimensional or special Borel examples do not cover the parameter family and both component dimensions.

value.rationale: The transition separates arithmetic dependence on the weight matroid from a geometric phenomenon: the dimension of the zero-toral fiber eventually forces another component, and the deformation proves this is the first possible threshold. Giving the exact components, dimensions and equidimensional boundary for a natural characteristic-independent family is useful beyond the routine rank expansion. The arithmetic count adds an explicit all-arity invariant rather than a collection of small field counts.
